title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: people data with source-system access controls
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets, existing connector controls and licensing statements are supported. It distinguishes the planned people-data permissions from today's everyone-access requirement and correctly leaves the new control's default and migration process unresolved.

claims.claim: This roadmap change concerns Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) people connectors.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Copilot People Connectors introduces people data ingestions with differentiated access control

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to import external people data together with its access control lists.
claims.quote: This release enables organizations to bring people data from external systems into Microsoft 365 along with associated access control lists (ACLs)

claims.claim: The planned capability makes Copilot respect the permissions defined in the source system.
claims.quote: ensuring Copilot respects existing permissions defined in source systems.

claims.claim: Imported people data can be scoped to specific individuals under the planned capability.
claims.quote: The imported data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups

claims.claim: Imported people data can be scoped to specific groups under the planned capability.
claims.quote: The imported data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups

claims.claim: Copilot will be able to reason over imported people data while honouring access restrictions.
claims.quote: allowing Copilot to reason over people data while honoring access restrictions.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Today's people connector data is visible to all tenant users by default.
claims.quote: By default, people data provided via a Copilot connector is visible to all users in the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Today's build guide requires an everyone ACL on ingested people items.
claims.quote: You must set the access control list (ACL) on items ingested by the connector to grant access to everyone.

claims.claim: The current people connector guides do not describe differentiated people ACLs, and no Learn page for this roadmap feature was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot people connectors access control ACL differentiated permissions licensing default; people data connectors differentiated ACL permissions default migration 561326. Opened graph/peopleconnectors and the build-connectors-with-people-data guide; both retain everyone access.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Custom people connectors are built using Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.
claims.quote: You build Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data in the same way that you build other Copilot connectors, by using the Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.

claims.claim: The value people is documented for contentCategory in the v1.0 externalConnection resource.
claims.quote: Possible values are: uncategorized, knowledgeBase, wikis, fileRepository, qna, crm, dashboard, people, media, email, messaging, meetingTranscripts, taskManagement, learningManagement, unknownFutureValue.

claims.claim: People connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.
claims.quote: This connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.

claims.claim: People connector data is stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: When you upload people data, each user's data attributes are scoped to their Microsoft 365 user profile and stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the planned ACL control's default state.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot people connectors access control ACL differentiated permissions licensing default; people connectors ACL default migration rollout permissions. Read the roadmap, graph/peopleconnectors and the build guide; their defaults concern today's people data, not the new ACL control.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether existing people connections change automatically when ACL support arrives.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors ACL default migration rollout permissions; people data connectors differentiated ACL permissions default migration 561326. Read the roadmap, graph/peopleconnectors and the build guide; no automatic conversion of existing connections is described.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: A migration process for existing everyone-ACL people connections to the planned differentiated ACLs is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors ACL default migration rollout permissions; people data connectors differentiated ACL permissions default migration 561326. Opened graph/peopleconnectors, the build guide and manage-access-permissions; only general delete-and-recreate guidance is present.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: General connector documentation says updating access permissions after connection creation is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The general access-permissions guide describes deleting and recreating a connection to change its visibility model, not migration of future people ACLs.
claims.quote: In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection. Recreate the connection using the Custom setup flow and explicitly configure access permissions.

claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 profile visibility and access controls apply to people connector data.
claims.quote: Within your organization, this data is treated as organizational content and is subject to existing Microsoft 365 profile visibility and access controls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: People connectors respect Microsoft Purview Information Barriers.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data comply with information barriers (IB) to ensure compliance across various platforms.

claims.claim: Today's people connector data can be surfaced by Copilot and people search.
claims.quote: Adding people data to Microsoft Graph makes it available to Microsoft 365 Copilot and people experiences such as the profile card and people search.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: How the planned scoped ACLs apply across profile cards, Org Explorer and search is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors differentiated ACL permissions default migration profile cards Org Explorer licensing price meter June 2027 561326. Read graph/peopleconnectors and the build guide; current people experiences are described, but future ACL enforcement across them is not.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how information barriers interact with the planned per-person ACLs.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot people connectors access control ACL differentiated permissions licensing default; people connectors ACL scoping admin setting PowerShell Microsoft Graph individuals groups. Read graph/peopleconnectors and the build guide; no new ACL/information-barrier interaction is stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts that do not match a Microsoft Entra user.
claims.quote: Nonmatched user accounts (userPrincipalName or externalDirectoryObjectId) are ignored.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.claim: The sources describe ingestion and grounding, not a new autonomous write-action capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot people connectors access control ACL differentiated permissions licensing default; people data connectors differentiated ACL permissions 561326. Read the roadmap, graph/peopleconnectors and the build guide; no autonomous write-action change is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: People data connections do not support staged connections, so that route cannot be used for a pilot.
claims.quote: Connections with people data don't support staged connections.

claims.claim: Microsoft separately advises piloting people connectors with a limited audience.
claims.quote: Before rollout, confirm governance, privacy, and admin requirements for your connector and pilot with a limited audience.

claims.claim: Users cannot edit the connector-ingested properties themselves.
claims.quote: All properties ingested via the people connectors are read-only.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends disabling user editing of overlapping properties to avoid edits not appearing on profile cards.
claims.quote: We recommend that you disable user editing of any properties that are also ingested via people connectors to avoid scenarios where user edits aren't displayed on the profile card due to the precedence model.

claims.quote: Searched: people connectors ACL scoping admin setting PowerShell Microsoft Graph individuals groups; externalConnection Permissions Copilot Visibility API beta. Read the build guide, peopleconnectors and externalConnection reference; generic item ACL APIs do not override the people everyone requirement.

claims.claim: Connector permissions can be viewed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Permissions.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane. Under Permissions, you can view the permissions set for the connector.

claims.claim: No API equivalent is documented for the connector-level Permissions view's source-ACL or everyone visibility model.

Read manage-access-permissions and the v1.0 externalConnection reference; no connector-level permission-model operation found.

claims.claim: The Permissions view is documented for each Microsoft 365 Copilot connector and distinguishes source ACLs from visibility to everyone.
claims.quote: You can review and validate access permissions for each Microsoft 365 Copilot connector from the connection details pane in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The general Copilot Visibility toggle is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connection > Copilot Visibility.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connection that you want to modify. Under Copilot Visibility, select the toggle to turn the connector on or off, and choose Save.

claims.claim: An automation operation equivalent to the Copilot Visibility toggle is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph external connection Copilot Visibility toggle API enabledContentExperiences Permissions view; externalConnection Permissions Copilot Visibility API beta. Read manage-connector, externalConnection reference and connection-management guide; no equivalent toggle property found.

claims.claim: The visibility guide describes partner connectors without specifically confirming the toggle for people connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph externalConnection Permissions Copilot Visibility API PowerShell people connector custom creation admin center. Read manage-connector and peopleconnectors; the toggle's stated scope is partner connectors, not all people connectors.

claims.claim: The cited people connector guides do not document admin UI creation of custom people connections.
claims.quote: Searched: custom people connectors admin center create connection. Read peopleconnectors, the people build guide and custom SDK publication search excerpt; generic SDK and federated creation routes do not document a people-specific connection configuration route.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections creates an external connection used by a people connector.
claims.quote: Create a new externalConnection object. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections

claims.claim: A connector can be deleted at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Delete.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane. In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection.

claims.claim: DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/{connectionId} deletes the external connection.
claims.quote: Deletes an externalConnection object. DELETE /external/connections/{connectionsId}. DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr

claims.claim: Deleting a people connector removes it and its connected data from Microsoft 365 instances, with delays possible.
claims.quote: If a connector is deleted, it's removed from all instances, but delays can be expected.

claims.claim: Existing connections can be inventoried at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 Admin Center, go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections.

claims.claim: The Graph connection-management article uses the alternative navigation label Copilot > Agents and connectors.
claims.quote: A search admin can view and manage all the connections in the tenant via the Copilot > Agents and connectors section of the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Skills, positions, addresses and phones are examples of supported people attributes that administrators can plan to map.
claims.quote: personCurrentPosition | string | workPosition; personAddresses | stringCollection | itemAddress; personPhones | stringCollection | itemPhone; personSkills | stringCollection | skillProficiency

claims.claim: The documented general Copilot Visibility toggle controls inclusion of connector data in Copilot Search and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: When the visibility is off, the connector is excluded from all Copilot Search and Copilot Chat results and responses.

claims.claim: A connector containing people data must set contentCategory to people.
claims.quote: Copilot connectors that contain people data must have the value people in the contentCategory property of the externalConnections API.
